guide_enrichment.narrative:
We do not see a meaningful model-market disagreement here. Our numbers favor Tennessee largely because its offense has two plausible paths to efficiency: a strong rushing profile against a more ordinary Texas run defense, and a passing game that grades better than the opposing pass defense. Texas has the clearer concern on the ground in our data, which could make sustaining drives more difficult if the passing game is not consistently productive.

We are not dismissing what Texas showed in its opener. Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns, while the offense produced 516 total yards. Texas also returns four offensive-line starters, so there is enough experience and passing-game upside to challenge our matchup lean. Add in a defense that forced at least one turnover in 36 of its previous 37 games, and we do not see enough separation from the market to justify the current price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Tennessee's rushing offense against Texas' run defense. Our efficiency numbers point to the Tennessee ground game as the clearest potential source of separation. The challenge is that Texas has consistently created extra possessions, including an SEC-leading 21 takeaways in 2025, so Tennessee's rushing advantage matters most if it can produce efficient drives without giving those possessions back.

recent_game.fact: Texas defeated Texas State 59-7 in its 2026 season opener on Sept. 5.
Texas produced 516 total yards and averaged 7.0 yards per play against Texas State.
Texas rushed for 156 yards and three touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas forced three turnovers—two fumbles and one interception—against Texas State.

opponent_notes.fact: Texas is scheduled to play Tennessee at 11 a.m. CT on Sept. 26, 2026, at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, with television coverage on ABC or ESPN.
The Tennessee game will be Texas' first trip to Knoxville.

quarterback.fact: Senior quarterback Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns against Texas State.
Manning is 13-3 as a starter and has appeared in 26 games with 16 starts at Texas.
In 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns while adding 399 rushing yards and a team-high 10 rushing touchdowns.
Over his final six games of 2025, Manning generated 1,714 passing yards, 205 rushing yards and 20 total touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas in spring 2026 from Arizona State and NC State, respectively.
Smothers had seven carries for 72 yards and caught three passes for 28 yards and a touchdown against Texas State.
Brown had 11 carries for 34 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Wide receiver Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and a touchdown against Texas State.
Wingo led Texas in 2025 with 54 receptions, 834 receiving yards and seven receiving touchdowns.
Wide receiver Cam Coleman transferred from Auburn in spring 2026 and caught three passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut.
Texas returns 2025 offensive-line starters Trevor Goosby, Brandon Baker, Cole Hutson and Connor Robertson.
Texas added offensive linemen Laurence Seymore III, Melvin Siani and Dylan Sikorski through the transfer portal for 2026.
The listed Texas offensive linemen entered 2026 with a combined 226 games played and 114 starts.
Tight end Michael Masunas transferred from Michigan State in spring 2026 after recording 19 catches for 232 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: Edge rusher Colin Simmons returned for his third season after leading Texas in 2025 with 15.5 tackles for loss, 12 sacks, 15 pressures and three forced fumbles.
Simmons recorded a half tackle for loss, a quarterback hurry and a fumble recovery against Texas State.

Texas added 2026 defensive transfers Rasheem Biles, Markus Boswell, Justin Cryer and Darius Snow at linebacker; Ian Geffrard and Zion Williams on the defensive line; and Nick Hudson and Bo Mascoe in the secondary.

coaching_changes.fact: Texas' 2026 staff lists Kyle Flood as offensive coordinator and offensive line coach, AJ Milwee as co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and Michael Bimonte as passing game coordinator and assistant quarterbacks coach.
Texas' 2026 staff lists Will Muschamp as defensive coordinator and Johnny Nansen as co-defensive coordinator and linebackers coach.

offensive_context.fact: Texas did not punt against Texas State, its first game without a punt since the 2023 game against Kansas.
Texas entered 2026 with Brown and Smothers both coming off at least 900 FBS rushing yards in 2025.
Texas was 26-2 when scoring first from the beginning of the 2023 season through its 2026 opener.

defensive_context.fact: Texas had 57 takeaways from the start of 2024 through its 2026 opener.
Texas forced at least one turnover in 36 of its previous 37 games through the 2026 opener.
Texas led the SEC with 21 takeaways in 2025 and ranked second in the conference with 16 interceptions.
Texas recorded at least 40 sacks and 15 interceptions in both 2024 and 2025.

special_teams.fact: Punter Mac Chiumento transferred to Texas from Florida State, kicker Gianni Spetic transferred from Memphis and deep snapper Trey Dubuc transferred from New Mexico for the 2026 season.

series_context.fact: Texas and Tennessee will meet for the fourth time and for the first time since 1969.
Texas leads the all-time series against Tennessee 2-1.

other_relevant.fact: Thirty-three players made their Texas debuts in the 59-7 win over Texas State.
Texas added 22 transfers from other colleges for the 2026 season.
